compliance_deadlines: 2020: Strategic milestone to align overall AI technology and applications with world-advanced levels and preliminarily establish AI ethical norms and policies/regulations in selected fields
2025: Strategic milestone to preliminarily establish an AI legal, regulatory, ethical, and policy system and form AI safety assessment and control capabilities
2030: Strategic milestone to reach world-leading levels in AI overall and build a more comprehensive AI legal, regulatory, ethical, and policy system
implementation_notes: Issued as State Council Notice Guo Fa [2017] No. 35 (dated 2017-07-08; published online 2017-07-20), this is China's overarching national AI strategy paper setting three-step targets for 2020, 2025, and 2030 rather than an enforceable statute. It directs ministries and local governments to implement R&D, industrial, military-civil fusion, infrastructure, and workforce tasks, coordinated by the National Leading Group for S&T System Reform and MOST (hosting the AI Plan Promotion Office) alongside an AI Strategic Advisory Committee. While it imposes no direct legal sanctions, Section 5 calls for future legislation on civil and criminal AI liability, sector-specific safety rules (e.g., autonomous driving, service robots), a dual-layer design-accountability and application-supervision regime, safety certification, and stronger penalties for data abuse, privacy infringement, and ethical violations.
